# Question 1

## For the Setup 

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_colour_viridis_d
scale_fill_discrete = scale_fill_viridis_d

data("ny_noaa")

```


## Data Description 

```{r}

ny_noaa |> 
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.)))) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "prop_missing") |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)
range(ny_noaa$date)

```
The dataset has `r format(nrow(ny_noaa), big.mark = ",")` rows and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` columns, with daily weather observations from ``r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)`` New York stations between 1981 and 2010 . Key variables include id (station), date, prcp (precipitation in tenths of mm), snow (snowfall in mm), snwd (snow depth in mm), and tmax/tmin (tenths of °C). Missingness is large, especially for tmax and tmin (found to be 44% each), snwd (23%), and snow (15%), while prcp is missing less often (6%). There are many stations that didn't record all variables, due to this the summaries need na.rm = TRUE. 

## Cleaning

```{r}

noaa_df = 
  ny_noaa |> 
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-", convert = TRUE) |> 
  mutate(
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10)

noaa_df |> 
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") |> 
  arrange(desc(n_obs))

```
The most commonly observed snowfall value is 0, because most days in New York have no snowfall. NA is the second most common (381,221 observations), as a lot of stations don't even record the snowfall. Among nonzero values, the most common are 25 mm, 13 mm, 51 mm and 76 mm. 

## Mean tmax by station in January and July 
```{r}
tmax_station_df = 
  noaa_df |> 
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |> 
  mutate(month = if_else(month == 1, "January", "July")) |> 
  group_by(id, month, year) |> 
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  ungroup()

tmax_station_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) + 
  geom_line(alpha = .3) + 
  facet_grid(. ~ month) + 
  labs(
    title = "Average max temperature by station, January vs. July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean max temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from the NY NOAA dataset"
  )

tmax_station_df |> 
  group_by(month) |> 
  filter(min_rank(mean_tmax) < 4)
```
The average max temperatures in January range from around (-13°C to 10°C), while July averages cluster between arounf 22°C and 32°C. Stations move together from year to year, with warm and cold years showing up across nearly all stations. This points to regional weather, rather than station-specific differences, as the main driver of the pattern. Both year-to-year and station-to-station variation are much greater in January than in July.The lowest values in each month stand out as outliers. In January, station USC00301723 in 1982 has the lowest average (-13.4°C), followed by USC00305925 in 2005 (-12.2°C) and USC00306957 in 2004 (-10.8°C). In July, station USC00308962 in 1988 has an average of 14.0°C, far below the typical range, and USC00302454 in 2004 (18.3°C) and USC00308946 in 1984 (19.1°C) are also unusually low.

## tmax vs tmin - snowfall by year 
```{r}
ggp_temp = 
  noaa_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_hex() + 
  scale_fill_continuous(breaks = c(10000, 30000, 50000)) + 
  labs(
    title = "Daily tmax vs. tmin",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) + 
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"))
ggp_snow = 
  noaa_df |> 
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, y = factor(year))) + 
  geom_density_ridges(scale = .85) + 
  scale_y_discrete(breaks = seq(1985, 2010, 5)) + 
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall distribution by year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year"
  )

ggp_temp + ggp_snow

```
The hex plot shows the density and this plot shows us that tmax and tmin are positively related.Most observations are concentrated in a single band roughly 10 to 25°C for both. The yearly snowfall distributions look very similar to one another. All are right-skewed. 

# Question 2 
```{r}

covar_df = 
  read_csv("./data/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  filter(age >= 21) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  mutate(
    sex = 
      case_match(
        sex, 
        1 ~ "male", 
        2 ~ "female"),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("male", "female")),
    education = 
      case_match(
        education, 
        1 ~ "Less than high school", 
        2 ~ "High school equivalent", 
        3 ~ "More than high school"),
    education = factor(
      education, 
      levels = c("Less than high school", "High school equivalent", "More than high school")))

accel_df = 
  read_csv("./data/nhanes_accel.csv") |> 
  janitor::clean_names()

nhanes_df = 
  left_join(covar_df, accel_df, by = "seqn")

```
